purpose: block-stratified error bars on the emission policy, on the catalogue and on the new-fault-like proxy population, from an exact additive decomposition of the official metric plus a block bootstrap

partition.assignment: greedy LPT: blocks dealt by descending fault mass to the fold with the smallest normalised load (fault/target + valid/target)

prediction.note: The input carries a continuous probability field, so both the floor and the width axis are measured.

restriction.note: only the blocks of fold 1 (the blocks held out from that fold's training); this is a generalisation reading ONLY if --pred came from a model trained with training.holdout=spatial_blocks and training.block_fold=1 on the same partition (block_px=512, folds=4, seed 0, mode balanced)

bootstrap.unit: spatial block, resampled with replacement, recomposed from the additive metric components

reliability.note: ONLY 9 independent resampling units (below 12), so the interval is COARSE: a bootstrap that redraws 9 blocks cannot separate a regional preference from sampling noise. A candidate whose contrast flips sign against the full-grid measurement is expected sampling variation at this sample size, NOT evidence that the policy should change; the global full-grid number remains the selection statistic. This happens whenever the measurement is restricted (--score-fold) or the footprint is small.
reliability.warning: sign flips against the full-grid run are sampling noise at 9 resampling units

provenance.definition: labels.tif fault pixels UNION proxy_catalogue.tif code-2 pixels, inside the footprint
provenance.surrogacy: surrogate for the Phase-2 'complete updated test set' (rules 3.6: the same submission is scored again against all fault labels in the set the expert panel updates after the competition closes).  It is NOT that set: the updated set is written by experts, partly FROM the predictions, so it can contain faults no free catalogue maps and can omit SGMC traces the panel rejects.
provenance.why_not_decomposable: FP_w is a sum over PREDICTION pixels of 1 - max_g k(d(x,g)), so the combined FP_w cannot be recomposed from the two component populations' FP_w (TP_w and FN_w can: both are sums over truth pixels, and the two truth sets are disjoint).  The combined population is therefore scored from the rasters, never inferred from the two committed reports.

combined_population.caveat: best_swept is a maximum over the swept grid ON THE JUDGING POPULATION: upward biased, never a shipping recommendation (the same caveat docs/FIELD_SELECTION_RULE.md records).  The combined population is a surrogate, not the Phase-2 set - see provenance.surrogacy.

interpretation.interpretation: DTI is not decomposable over blocks: TP_w sums over truth pixels while the FP penalty is a global mass term, so a candidate can win in most blocks and still lose globally.  Per-block numbers are for VARIANCE (the block bootstrap) and for locating where a score comes from; the global DTI stays the selection statistic.  This run measured that conflict: floor0.3_w0px wins 5/9 blocks but loses globally (0.1397 < 0.1450)

verdict.note: Candidates are derived from the SHIPPED raster, so floors below the applied floor and un-thinned variants are not recoverable here; the runner sweep (.github/workflows/proxy-eval.yml) covers those.  Per-block catalogue DTI is in-domain (the shipped model trained on every label); per-block proxy-only DTI is not, because those pixels are absent from the training labels by construction.

pruning.rule: per-block rows dropped only for emissions that duplicate another candidate's emission; global numbers and the twin reference kept
pruning.applied_after: bootstrap, sign agreement, verdict and the reproduction check (none of which read a duplicate's rows)
